question: Claude has generated a project proposal as a Markdown document artifact. The user wants to tighten the wording of just the second paragraph without regenerating the whole document or losing the original version. What should the user do?
options: A) Ask Claude to generate a second, separate artifact containing only the revised paragraph, as artifacts are static after creation and lack any editing interface.
B) Use the inline "Edit with Claude" feature on the Markdown artifact to revise the paragraph; the feature creates a new version and keeps the original accessible.
C) Delete the artifact and ask Claude to regenerate the entire proposal. Artifacts are locked once created and cannot accept paragraph modifications.
D) Copy the entire document into the chat as plain text and manually retype the corrected paragraph. Artifacts cannot accept partial edits once created.
correct_answers: B) Use the inline "Edit with Claude" feature on the Markdown artifact to revise the paragraph; the feature creates a new version and keeps the original accessible.
explanations: Incorrect. Artifacts are not static; they have an editing interface. Asking for a separate artifact would clutter the workspace and miss the versioning capability of the built-in editor.

Correct. The inline "Edit with Claude" feature on a Markdown artifact allows you to make targeted revisions like tightening a single paragraph. It creates a new version while preserving the original, so the user can compare or revert if needed.
Incorrect. Artifacts are not locked once created; they support inline editing. Deleting and regenerating the entire proposal is unnecessary for a single paragraph change.
Incorrect. The artifact does not need to be copied out and manually retyped. Users can edit artifacts directly within the interface, so partial edits are possible without leaving the artifact.
